result.summary:
Wrote docs/agents/design/REQ-029.md: QR check-in via a plain-phone-camera scan delivering /start ci_<qr_token> from the VOLUNTEER's own Telegram account -- the full 5-row refusal table (S5), the S4 token-scope/expiry enforcement, S3's phone/email exclusion, and the organizer-override transition with its own logged AuditLog row.

SCHEMA CHECK (Sec0, mandatory pre-check) -- NO CHANGE NEEDED, confirmed by direct inspection of db/schema.ts: qr_token (text) already exists with a unique index (registrations_qr_token_unique, line 287) -- a token lookup is already an indexed equality lookup. checked_in_at/checked_in_by/check_in_method and the chk_registrations_checked_in_only_if_admitted CHECK constraint (S6) all already exist (REQ-011/022/028). generateQrToken (REQ-020) already produces a 256-bit CSPRNG token (S4). DATA-DESIGNER does NOT run this cycle.

DEEP-LINK WIRING (Sec1): parseStartPayload's StartPayload union gains a `{ kind: "checkin"; qrToken }` member via a new `ci_` prefix branch (checked before the existing `e_` branch), stated as a grammar table. makeStartHandler (start.ts) gets a second dispatch branch alongside the existing `payload.kind === "event"` check, calling a NEW resolveCheckinQrDeepLink (handlers/checkinQr.ts, new file) with the scanner resolved via the ordinary ctx.from.id -> flowUser.id path already running at the top of that handler -- never via the token. Explicitly reasoned why this branch needs NO consent gate (unlike the event branch): it writes nothing new about the scanner, matching every existing staff/organizer action's precedent in this codebase.

DECISION FUNCTION -- NEW, not a reuse of REQ-028's decideCheckinToggleOutcome (Sec3.1 states the reasoning explicitly): three structural mismatches -- (1) QR must NEVER undo a check-in on a repeat scan (REQ-028's 4th branch would silently clear checked_in_at, which AC2 forbids), (2) the refusal needs a per-admission-state specific reason string plus an override offer REQ-028's table has no concept of, (3) check_in_method must be 'qr' not toggleCheckIn's hardcoded 'manual'. New decideQrCheckinOutcome (4-row table: unknown-token / refused-not-admitted / already-checked-in / check-in) and performQrCheckIn (transactional write) designed in Sec3, mirroring toggleCheckIn's row-lock-then-decide-then-write skeleton exactly.

S4 TOKEN-CURRENCY RECHECK (Sec3.3 step 2, no REQ-028 equivalent): the transactional write's fresh locked SELECT re-checks that the row's qr_token still equals the token this call was invoked with -- a registration re-issued a new token (e.g. withdraw-then-re-register) is treated as unknown-token even though the same registration id still resolves, closing the gap where a stale/superseded printed QR could keep working via an id-based re-lookup.

AUDIT-NAMES-THE-REGISTRATION EXTENSION (Sec5): AC1 requires the non-staff refusal's audit row to name the actor, action, AND the registration -- REQ-018/028's existing requireEventStaffForEvent/buildCheckinRefusalAudit write entity:'event'/entityId:eventId (no registration in play at their call sites). Extended BOTH functions with one new OPTIONAL registrationId parameter, backward-compatible (every existing REQ-018/028 call site passes nothing, byte-for-byte unaffected) -- when supplied, entity becomes 'registration'/entityId becomes registrationId. Flagged explicitly as the one modification to a previously-reviewed file this requirement needs, with the reasoning for why it's unavoidable (this is the only code path that writes this specific audit row).

ORGANIZER OVERRIDE (Sec4): a NEW state transition (registration.ts's overrideAdmitAndCheckIn) -- pure decideOverrideOutcome (3-row table: not-found / already-admitted / override-admit) explicitly does NOT re-run decideRegistrationOutcome's capacity gate (S7 names this exact transition as the ONE way seats_taken may exceed capacity, so re-checking capacity here would contradict the invariant it exists to satisfy) -- registerForEvent is correctly NOT reused for this reason, stated explicitly. One UPDATE (admission->'admitted' AND checked_in_at/checked_in_by/check_in_method='manual' in the SAME statement) + exactly one writeAuditLog call, one transaction (AC6). Authorization is requireOrganizerForChapter (REQ-016, reused byte-for-byte unchanged) against the event's chapterId -- deliberately STRICTER than the scanning EventStaff check, reasoned via S2 (EventStaff's rights are check-in-only, 'nothing else'; overriding capacity/waitlist rules is an organizer decision) and cross-checked against REQ-030's independent same-conclusion design for the structurally identical 'admit past normal rules' action. The override button's tap re-authorizes the TAPPING user (not the original scanner) at tap time.

AC5/S3 (Sec2.1): getRegistrationByQrTokenForCheckin's SELECT clause structurally never names profiles.phone/profiles.email -- reuses REQ-028's existing displayName derivation table by exporting the previously-private deriveCheckinDisplayName helper (a plumbing change, not new logic) rather than re-deriving the same rule twice.

All 7 ACs mapped to concrete design elements in Sec10. 4 open questions stated explicitly in Sec9: whether 'rejected' registrations should get the override offer (ACs don't test this state; included by structural analogy, flagged as unconfirmed); the real-world workflow when the scanner tapping Override is not themselves an organizer (left as an operational question, not a code question); the override success screen's exact message-editing mechanic (no AC distinguishes edit-in-place vs. new reply); which existing one-line read resolves the scanner's own users.id inside the handler (either existing option is acceptable). Sec8 confirms no Mini App/WebApp/custom-client code path is introduced anywhere -- the only new entry point is parseStartPayload's ci_ branch, reached solely through Telegram's own deep-link mechanism (AC7).
result.next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (Step 1b) -- DATA-DESIGNER does not run this cycle, no stored-data change (qr_token, its unique index, checked_in_at/checked_in_by/check_in_method, and the S6 CHECK constraint all already exist from prior requirements). Note for CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR: Sec5 modifies two existing, previously-reviewed functions in domain/eventStaffAuthorization.ts (an additive, backward-compatible optional parameter) -- verify this is the narrowest change that satisfies AC1's 'names the registration' wording, not scope creep.
